source_text: Καὶ πάλιν ὡς αὐτολεξεὶ διὰ παρθένου μὲν τεχθησόμενος διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου προεφητεύθη, ἀκούσατε. Ἐλέχθη δὲ οὕτως· „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ ἐροῦσιν ἐπὶ τᾷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός“. Ἃ γὰρ ἦν ἄπιστα καὶ ἀδύνατα νομιζόμενα παρὰ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις γενήσεσθαι, ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς προεμήνυσε διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος μέλλειν γίνεσθαι, ἵνα ὅταν γένηται μὴ ἀπιστηθῇ, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ προειρῆσθαι πιστευθῇ. Ὅπως δὲ μή τινες, μὴ νοήσαντες τὴν δεδηλωμένην προφητείαν, ἐγκαλέσωσιν ἡμῖν ἅπερ ἐνεκαλέσαμεν τοῖς ποιηταῖς, εἰποῦσιν ἀφροδισίων χάριν ἐληλυθέναι ἐπὶ γυναῖκας τὸν Δία, διασαφῆσαι τοὺς λόγους πειρασόμεθα. Τὸ οὖν „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει“ σημαίνει οὐ συνουσιασθεῖσαν τὴν παρθένον συλλαβεῖν· εἰ γὰρ ἐσυνουσιάσθη ὑπὸ ὁτουοῦν, οὐκ ἔτι ἦν παρθένος· ἀλλὰ δύναμις θεοῦ ἐπελθοῦσα τῇ παρθένῳ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτήν, καὶ κυοφορῆσαι παρθένον οὖσαν πεποίηκε. Καὶ ὁ ἀποσταλεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν τὴν παρθένον κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνο τοῦ καιροῦ ἄγγελος θεοῦ εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτὴν εἰπών· „Ἰδοὺ συλλήψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ υἱὸς ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“, ὡς οἱ ἀπομνημονεύσαντες πάντα τὰ περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐδίδαξαν, οἷς ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προδεδηλωμένου τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα τοῦτον γεννησόμενον, ὡς προεμηνύομεν, ἔφη. Τὸ πνεῦμα οὖν καὶ. τὴν δύναμιν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδὲν ἄλλο νοῆσαι θέμις ἢ τὸν λόγον, ὃς καὶ πρωτότοκος τῷ θεῷ ἐστι, Μωϋσῆς ὁ προδεδηλωμένος προφήτης ἐμήνυσε· καὶ τοῦτο ἐλθὸν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον καὶ ἐπισκιάσαν οὐ διὰ συνουσίας ἀλλὰ διὰ δυνάμεως ἐγκύμονα κατέστησε. Τὸ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, ὄνομα τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ, σωτὴρ τῇ ἑλληνίδι διαλέκτῳ δηλοῖ. Ὅθεν καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς τὴν παρθένον εἶπε· „Καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν· αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“. Ὅτι δὲ οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ θεοφοροῦνται οἱ προφητεύοντες εἰ μὴ λόγῳ θείῳ, καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὡς ὑπολαμβάνω, φήσετε.
pass_a_gloss: And again, as it was spoken by God, He who was to be born through a virgin was foretold by Isaiah, listen. It was said in this way: 'Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which is God with us.' For what seemed unbelievable and impossible to men, God foretold through the prophetic Spirit that it would happen, so that when it happens, it may not be disbelieved, but believed because it was foretold. So that some may not, not understanding the given prophecy, accuse us of what we accused the poets, saying that Zeus came to women for the sake of lust, we will try to clarify the words. The phrase 'Behold, the virgin will have in her womb' means that the virgin, not having intercourse, conceived; for if she had intercourse with anyone, she would no longer be a virgin; but the power of God, coming upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and made her, still a virgin, pregnant. And the angel sent to the virgin at that time announced the good news to her, saying: 'Behold, you will conceive in your womb from the Holy Spirit and bear a son, and he will be called the son of the Most High, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins,' as those who remembered all things about our Savior Jesus Christ taught, whom we believed, since also through Isaiah, the prophet who previously spoke, the prophetic Spirit said that he would be born, as we foretold. The Spirit, therefore, and the power from God, it is not right to understand as anything else but the Word, who is also the firstborn of God, as Moses, the previously mentioned prophet, foretold; and this, coming upon the virgin and overshadowing her, not through intercourse but through power, made her pregnant. The name Jesus, in the Hebrew language, means Savior in the Greek dialect. From which also the angel said to the virgin: 'And you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.' That the prophets do not prophesy carrying any other god but the divine Word, you also, I suppose, will say.

pass_b_english: And again, as God spoke it, the one who was to be born through a virgin was foretold by Isaiah: listen. The prophecy ran thus: "Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel," which means God with us (Isaiah 7:14). For the things that seemed unbelievable and impossible to human beings, God foretold through the prophetic Spirit that they would come to pass, so that when they happen they may not be disbelieved, but may be believed because they were foretold. In order that no one might, failing to understand the prophecy that has been set forth, accuse us of the very charge we leveled against the poets — saying that Zeus came to women for the sake of lust — we will try to clarify the words. The phrase "Behold, the virgin will have in her womb" means that the virgin conceived without having intercourse; for if she had intercourse with anyone, she would no longer be a virgin, but the power of God, coming upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and made her pregnant while she remained a virgin. And the angel of God sent to the virgin at that time announced the good news to her, saying: "Behold, you will conceive in your womb from the Holy Spirit and bear a son, and he will be called the Son of the Most High, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins," just as those who remembered all things concerning our Savior Jesus Christ taught, in whom we believed, since also through Isaiah, the prophet who previously spoke, the prophetic Spirit said that he would be born, as we foretold. Therefore, it is not right to understand the Spirit and the power from God as anything other than the Word, who is also the firstborn of God, as Moses, the prophet previously mentioned, foretold; and this Word, coming upon the virgin and overshadowing her, made her pregnant not through intercourse but through power. The name Jesus, in the Hebrew language, means Savior in the Greek tongue. From which the angel also said to the virgin: "And you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins." That the prophets do not prophesy carrying any other god but the divine Word — you also, I suppose, will say.
